source_text: Ταῦτα δὲ παραινῶ ὑμῖν, ἀγαπητοί, εἰδὼς ὅτι καὶ ὑμεῖς οὕτως ἔχετε. προφυλάσσω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τῶν θηρίων τῶν ἀνθρωπομόρφων, οὓς οὐ μόνον δεῖ ὑμᾶς μὴ παραδέχεσθαι, ἀλλ’ εἰ δυνατὸν μηδὲ συναντᾶν, μόνον δὲ προσεύχεσθε ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν, ἐάν πως μετανοήσωσιν, ὅπερ δύσκολον, τούτου δὲ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, τὸ ἀληθινὸν ἡμῶν ζῆν. 2, εἰ γὰρ τὸ δοκεῖν ταῦτα ἐπράχθη ὑπὸ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν, κἀγὼ τὸ δοκεῖν δέδεμαι. τί δὲ καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἔκδοτον δέδωκα τῷ θανάτῳ, πρὸς πῦρ, πρὸς μάχαιραν, πρὸς θηρία; ἀλλ’ ἐγγὺς μαχαίρας ἐγγὺς θεοῦ, μεταξὺ θηρίων μεταξὺ θεοῦ: μόνον ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς τὸ συμπαθεῖν αὐτῷ πάντα ὑπομένω, αὐτοῦ με ἐνδυναμοῦντος τοῦ τελείου ἀνθρώπου.
thought_title: Warning against human-shaped beasts and the reality of his bonds
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Smyrnaeans, warning them against false teachers who deny the real flesh of Christ, and now turns to his own imprisonment as proof that Christ's suffering was real.
pass_a_gloss: These things [I] urge you, beloved, knowing that also you thus hold. [I] guard before you from the beasts in human form, whom not only it is necessary you not receive, but if possible not even meet, only but pray on behalf of them, if somehow they repent, which [is] difficult, of this but has authority Jesus Christ, the true life of us. For if in mere appearance these things were done by the Lord of us, I also in mere appearance am bound. Why also myself given over have I given to death, to fire, to sword, to beasts? But near sword near God, between beasts between God: only in the name of Jesus Christ for the suffering-with him all things I endure, him empowering me, the perfect man.

choices.why: Keeps the literal compound adjective and the dehumanizing force of calling false teachers beasts

choices.english: I am guarding you in advance
choices.why: The verb means to guard beforehand; the present tense is rendered progressively to show ongoing warning
Fixed glossary term for the false claim that Christ only seemed to suffer

choices.english: Near the sword means near God
choices.why: The elliptical parallel is expanded with 'means' to make the aphorism clear in English while keeping its force
rejected: close to the sword, close to God

choices.english: so that I may suffer with him
choices.why: The purpose clause is made explicit; 'suffer with' preserves the compound verb's sense of shared suffering
Keeps the genitive absolute as a descriptor of Christ, the one empowering Ignatius

pass_b_english: I urge these things on you, beloved, knowing that you too hold the same conviction. But I am guarding you in advance against the beasts in human form. You must not only refuse to welcome them; if possible, do not even meet them. Only pray for them, in case they might somehow repent, though that is difficult. Yet Jesus Christ, our true life, has power over this.

For if these things were done by our Lord in mere appearance, then I too am bound in mere appearance. And why have I handed myself over to death, to fire, to the sword, to beasts? No: to be near the sword is to be near God; to be among beasts is to be among God. Only in the name of Jesus Christ do I endure everything, so that I may suffer with him, since the perfect man empowers me.

problems.quote: Near the sword means near God; among beasts means among God
problems.source_quote: ἀλλ’ ἐγγὺς μαχαίρας ἐγγὺς θεοῦ, μεταξὺ θηρίων μεταξὺ θεοῦ
problems.why: Missing 'but' (ἀλλ') and 'means' is interpretive; Greek is elliptical: 'near sword, near God; among beasts, among God.'
problems.fix: But near the sword is near God; among beasts is among God.
problems.ruling: ἀλλ' ('but') omitted; 'means' adds interpretive filler not in elliptical Greek ἐγγὺς μαχαίρας ἐγγὺς θεοῦ.

edits.old: Near the sword means near God; among beasts means among God.
edits.new: But near the sword is near God; among beasts is among God.

problems.why: Genitive τοῦ...ἀνθρώπου depends on ἐνδυναμοῦντος: 'the perfect man empowering me.' English makes it apposition: 'he empowers me—the perfect man,' which changes syntax but arguably not meaning. However, 'the perfect man' as apposition to Jesus is theologically loaded; the Greek has 'since the perfect man empowers me.'
problems.fix: since the perfect man empowers me
problems.ruling: τοῦ τελείου ἀνθρώπου is genitive subject of ἐνδυναμοῦντος: 'the perfect man empowers me,' not apposition to Christ.

edits.old: since he empowers me—the perfect man.
edits.new: since the perfect man empowers me.

fixed: The mistranslation about 'the perfect man' is real: the genitive depends on 'empowering,' so the English should read 'since the perfect man empowers me.'

problems.why: Oxymoron may confuse; means people who appear human but act like beasts.
Different animal metaphors for false teachers may blur into literal beasts of martyrdom.
problems.fix: Clarify which are metaphorical vs. literal where ambiguity arises.

fixed: The 'rabid dogs' problem is not present in this passage; no such phrase occurs in the English or source. The only animal metaphor here is 'beasts in human form,' which is now clarified as metaphorical for false teachers, distinct from the literal beasts of martyrdom mentioned later in the same sentence.

problems.quote: near the sword is near God; among beasts is among God
problems.why: Paradoxical formulation is unclear; seems to say proximity to death is proximity to God.
problems.fix: Revise to 'to be near the sword is to be near God; to be among beasts is to be among God'.

problems.why: 'Beasts' is used both for literal arena animals and metaphorically for false teachers; reader may conflate them.

edits.old: near the sword is near God; among beasts is among God
edits.new: to be near the sword is to be near God; to be among beasts is to be among God

fixed: The paradox is clarified by making the infinitive construction explicit, matching the source's elliptical contrast (ἐγγὺς μαχαίρας ἐγγὺς θεοῦ, μεταξὺ θηρίων μεταξὺ θεοῦ).

The glossary problem is not a translation error: 'beasts' in 1.7 is already 'beasts in human form' (τῶν θηρίων τῶν ἀνθρωπομόρφων), which distinguishes it from the literal beasts in 4.4–5. No edit needed.

last_rejected.quote: since the perfect man empowers me
last_rejected.source_quote: αὐτοῦ με ἐνδυναμοῦντος τοῦ τελείου ἀνθρώπου
last_rejected.why: Genitive absolute misread as causative; 'the perfect man' should be Christ, 'him empowering me'.
last_rejected.fix: with him, the perfect man, empowering me
last_rejected.ruling: Genitive absolute with αὐτοῦ can render as causal 'since'; 'the perfect man' is correctly identified as Christ empowering him.

last_rejected.quote: so that I may suffer with him
last_rejected.why: εἰς τὸ + infinitive expresses purpose ('in order to'), but 'so that I may' weakens the direct purpose.
last_rejected.fix: in order to suffer with him
last_rejected.ruling: 'So that I may suffer with him' adequately expresses purpose of εἰς τὸ συμπαθεῖν αὐτῷ; no meaning lost.

polish.changed: Clarified that the 'beasts in human form' are false teachers, not the literal beasts of martyrdom, and kept the contrast between mere appearance and real suffering explicit.

notes.fix: Clarify metaphor vs. literal where possible.

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker and referents, tightened sentence flow, and made the contrast in the second paragraph explicit with 'No:' so the reader hears Ignatius rejecting the 'mere appearance' logic.

notes.why: Same opponents described with different animal metaphors across letters; could confuse.
notes.fix: Note these are metaphorical descriptions of the same false teachers.
